headline: 30 Google ads for a clean-label baby brand - but the parent's first question is unanswered in the ad.
ad_intro: Early Foods is a Bengaluru clean-label baby and toddler food brand running 30 live Google creatives under Early Foods Pvt Ltd - a solid paid base in a category where trust is the entire purchase decision. The brand also runs a global storefront (global.earlyfoods.com). The leak is message-to-proof mapping: parents buy after they see ingredients, age-appropriateness and safety, yet the ad and landing path lead with the product rather than the reassurance stack that removes fear.
ad_intelligence: 30 live creatives; advertiser Early Foods Pvt Ltd.
Shopify storefront with a global store (global.earlyfoods.com) - i.e. international shipping is already live, which is an unusual growth channel for an Indian baby-food brand.

Indian baby-food is dominated by legacy multinationals on shelf; D2C challengers win on clean-label proof (no preservatives, no added sugar, millet-based, made fresh) plus trust signals - certifications, ingredient transparency, and parent reviews.

First-time parents research heavily before the first order and repurchase on subscription for 18-36 months. First-order CAC is amortised over a long, predictable LTV - so conversion rate at the first touch matters more than in almost any other food category.
findings: Fear is the real competitor: parents do not compare you to another brand - they compare the risk of trying you to the safety of a known multinational. The ad and page should open with the reassurance stack: age-appropriate, ingredient list, how it is made, what is NOT in it, and parent proof.
No visible parent UGC engine: the highest-converting asset in baby food is another parent's face and words. There is no visible system to collect, permission, and rotate parent videos into ads.
First-order friction: in a research-heavy category, a trial pack / sampler bundle with a clear 'start here by age' path converts far better than a full-price single SKU.

Retention not monetised: baby food is an 18-36 month subscription habit. A stage-based flow (6m/9m/12m/18m) with WhatsApp reminders and auto-replenish is the highest-margin system you could build - and it is not visible today.
competitors: Shelf ubiquity and grandmother-level brand trust.
Attack on ingredients: clean label, no preservatives, no refined sugar - with proof on the page.
Win with stage-based bundles, parent UGC, and global shipping proof.
Position as 'homemade, without the work' with ingredient transparency.
wins: Rebuild the ad-to-page path around the reassurance stack: age selector, full ingredient list, 'what's not inside' panel, certifications, and parent reviews above the fold. Route each ad to the matching age page, not the homepage.

Offer a starter bundle to 50 existing customers in exchange for a 20-second video ('what I feed my 10-month-old'). Rotate the top 12 as paid creatives monthly - real faces, real kitchens, zero production cost.
Build 6m / 9m / 12m / 18m bundles with auto-replenish, WhatsApp reminders and a 'grow with us' upgrade path. Baby food is a two-year subscription - price it like one.
impact: New channel at low incremental cost
